main_text.p: tus iusto Dei iudicio responderet. Vnde Mantua-nus:

p.i: Ad Romam conuerte oculos, luxumq; fluentem Aspice, & indignos Christi propagine mores. Tota in capreolos it uinea: tota comantem Effluit in syluam, foliis spargentibus umbram Pestiferam scegeti[?]: dulces neq; parturit uuas. Hos steriles ramos, nemus istud inutile, trunca.

main_text.p: Ab hoc Satanæ uicario, Ioanne 12[?]. Dunstanus monachus necromanticus, Archiepiscopus Cantua-riensis in Anglia, confirmationem, ac metropolis suæ pallium Romæ suscepit, anno Domini 960. Multa etiam pecuniæ summa, ab eodem obtinuit diabolo, magnæ authoritatis diploma: quo posset ministrorum Ecclesiæ coniugia damnare, & adpellere[?] pistici cœlibatus uotum compellere, aut omni prop-sus Ecclesiastico proventu exuere. Vide Ioannem Capgrauum in Catalogo sanctorum Angliæ, ac Po-lydorum Vergilium, lib. 6. Anglicæ historiæ. Inde Satanicus impostor, Edgari regis authoritate fre-tus, anno sequente, adiunctis sibi in eadem commis-sione, Osuualdo Eboracensi, atq; Ethelwaldo Vuintoniensi Episcopis, & similium artium mona-chis, sacerdotes omnes (quos uasa fornicationum hypocrita uocabat) cum non uellent uxores re-linquere, à cathedralibus Ecclesijs una cum ipsis uxoribus

page.notes: The line ends "Mantua-" / "nus:" and "Cantua-" / "riensis" are read as printed hyphens, though the hyphen is faint. "adpellere" and "pstici" / "pistici" (the line beginning "pistici cœlibatus") are doubtful and marked where the reading was least certain. "scegeti" in the verse is doubtful. "12" after "Ioanne" is read as a numeral and is marked [?]. Several lines are faded or show-through from the reverse, particularly on the right edge; the transcription of those lines is marked where the letters are unclear. The verse is printed in italic and is one stanza.
